title: Actor, Judge, or Teacher? Understanding Decision Models in Long-Horizon Agents
abstract: arXiv:2611.17167v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Decision models answer a question with a typed output, such as a choice among options with a probability for each, so one model can choose an agent's actions, evaluate actions already taken, or score every action to teach a policy with reinforcement learning. Prior work has studied them mainly as actors, judging their usefulness by how well they act. We ask whether a decision model that acts poorly can still teach well. We compare three decision models and three general LLMs as actors and judges on ALFWorld, and use JEV as a teacher on ALFWorld and WebShop. As actors, all six models are pulled away from a subgoal that must come first by an easier one. As judges that see the whole trajectory, the same models credit the steps toward that subgoal, and asking whether each action helped, rather than whether the task will succeed, separates useful from useless actions. As a teacher, JEV raises a Qwen2.5-1.5B policy over GRPO from 72.8% to 82.9

translated_title: 演员、裁判还是老师？理解长时程智能体中的决策模型
translated_abstract: 决策模型以类型化的输出回答问题，例如在多个选项中做出选择并为每个选项给出概率，因此同一个模型可以决定智能体的动作、评估已执行的动作，或对每个动作打分以便通过强化学习来训练策略。先前的工作主要将其作为“演员”来研究，以其行动表现的好坏来评判其价值。我们提出的问题是：一个行动表现不佳的决策模型是否仍能很好地进行“教学”？我们在 ALFWorld 上将三个决策模型和三个通用大语言模型作为演员和裁判进行比较，并将 JEV 作为教师应用于 ALFWorld 和 WebShop。作为演员时，所有六个模型都会被一个更容易的子目标吸引，从而偏离必须优先完成的子目标。而作为能看到完整轨迹的裁判时，同样的模型却会对朝向该子目标的步骤给予肯定评价，并且询问“每个动作是否有帮助”而非“任务是否会成功”，可以有效区分有用与无用的动作。作为教师时，JEV 将 Qwen2.5-1.5B 策略相较 GRPO 从 72.8% 提升至 82.9%。
tldr: 该研究发现行动表现不佳的决策模型仍可以是优秀的裁判和教师——JEV 作为教师将 Qwen2.5-1.5B 策略相较 GRPO 基线从 72.8% 提升至 82.9%，且以“每个动作是否有帮助”而非“任务是否成功”来评判轨迹，能有效区分有用与无用的动作。
en_tdlr: This study shows that a decision model that acts poorly can still judge and teach well: JEV as a teacher lifts a Qwen2.5-1.5B policy from 72.8% to 82.9% over GRPO, and evaluating each action's helpfulness rather than task success effectively separates useful from useless actions.
